story.head: Something has to give
paras: The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Nashville on Oct 13. The Golden Knights have won two in a row, and the Predators have won three straight. Going in, the Predators are fifth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (fifth).

The Predators’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.525), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Golden Knights’ record (.667) is about what their chances are worth.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (31st), so the Golden Knights keep shots away, but them give up plenty. The Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away (2nd). The Golden Knights’ power play against the Predators’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Filip Forsberg (5 G / 14 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Steven Stamkos (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals. Jack Eichel (7 G / 16 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Mark Stone (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL.

Juuse Saros (4-3-4 / .908 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Nashville. Vegas has two options in net: Carter Hart (5-3-2 / .900 SV% in 10 GS) and Adin Hill (6-2-0 / .895 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hart got the last one on Nov 5. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Ryan Craig likes to send Barbashev, Karlsson and Marner out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque. One more thing: the Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
